explication:
<explanation>
1. Project Type and Purpose  
   - This is a full-stack, terminal-based AI agent split into two main processes:  
     a. A **CLI client** (`app/cli`) used by developers to interact via REPL or commands.  
     b. A **Server** (`app/server`) providing HTTP/gRPC APIs, state management, database persistence, syntax parsing, and integration with AI model providers.

2. Main Components to Include in the Diagram  
   - CLI Client  
     • REPL / command parser / UI (TUI)  
     • Local cache and file-map modules  
   - Server API  
     • HTTP/gRPC endpoint layer (handlers, routes)  
     • Domain logic (plans, contexts, streams)  
     • Syntax & file-map service (tree-sitter)  
     • AI orchestration (litellm_proxy, batching, streaming)  
     • Email & notification service  
     • Shutdown / health check endpoints  
   - Data Store  
     • Relational DB (Postgres via `app/server/db`)  
     • Migrations  
   - External Services  
     • AI Model Providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, OpenRouter, etc.)  
     • Email SMTP or API  
     • Git (for file diffs, branch management)  

3. Relationships and Data Flows  
   - CLI → Server: REST or gRPC calls for all actions (`apply`, `plan`, `stream`, `auth`, etc.)  
   - Server → DB: CRUD operations, transactions, queue & locks  
   - Server → AI Providers: HTTP/HTTPS requests for context loading, prompts, streaming responses  
   - Server → Syntax Module: Local function calls for project map generation & structured edits  
   - Server → Email: Outbound notifications (invites, verification)  
   - Server → Git: File diffs, commit generation, branch operations  
   - Server → CLI: Server streams back events, logs, diffs, summaries  

4. Key Architectural Patterns  
   - **Separation of Concerns**: CLI and Server are distinct processes, communicate over an API.  
   - **Hexagonal Architecture**: Handlers → Domain → Adapters (DB, AI providers, syntax).  
   - **Event / Stream Processing**: Plans and build executions are streamed to the CLI.  
   - **Plugin-style Model Providers**: Shared interfaces for models; concrete implementations in `app/shared/ai_models_*`.  
   - **Cumulative Diff Sandbox**: All file edits are staged until approved, enabling rollbacks.  

5. Diagramming Guidelines  
   - Use **boxes** or **swimlanes** for each major component (CLI, Server, DB, External).  
   - Draw **arrows** to show request/response flows and streaming directions.  
   - **Color-code** components: e.g.,  
     • Blue = CLI  
     • Green = Server modules  
     • Orange = Database  
     • Purple = External AI/email services  
   - **Label** arrows with protocol or action (e.g., HTTP POST /plan, SQL SELECT, “stream tokens”).  
   - Use **dashed lines** for asynchronous or streaming flows (e.g., plan execution).  

6. ASCII-style Workflow Diagram Example  

          ┌───────────────────┐
          │   Developer CLI   │  <── Interactive REPL, commands
          │ (app/cli REPL/UI) │
          └────────┬──────────┘
                   │ HTTP/gRPC (REST endpoints)
                   ▼
          ┌────────────────────────────────────┐
          │            Server API             │
          │ (handlers, routes, auth, plans)   │
          └───┬─────────┬─────────┬───────────┘
              │         │         │
      ┌───────▼─┐   ┌───▼────┐  ┌─▼────────┐
      │  DB     │   │ Syntax │  │  AI      │
      │(Postgres│   │Service │  │Providers │
      │ migrations)│ (tree-sitter)│(OpenAI,  │
      └─────────┘   └────────┘   │Anthropic)│
           ▲                         └────▲────┘
           │ Email / Git               │
           │ notifications              │ prompt/stream
           └───────────────────────────┘

7. Tailoring to This Project’s Workflow  
   - Highlight the **“cumulative diff sandbox”** between CLI and file system.  
   - Show the **plan lifecycle**:  
     a. `plan create` request → server stores plan in DB  
     b. AI prompt cycle → streaming diff updates → sandbox  
     c. plan apply → server executes commands in controlled cgroups  
     d. commit & cleanup → Git integration  
   - Emphasize the **model orchestration** layer in `app/shared` and the local proxy (`litellm_proxy.py`).  

8. Final Tips  
   - Keep the diagram at **two levels**:  
     • High-level (CLI / Server / DB / External)  
     • Zoom-in view on Server internals (adapters, domain, handlers)  
   - Use **icons** or **shapes** to distinguish sync vs. async flows.  
   - Include a **legend** for colors, line-styles, and component types.  

This workflow diagram and guidelines will help you capture the essential architecture of Plandex, showing how the CLI client, server core, database, and external AI and email services interact to deliver a robust AI coding agent.  
</explanation>
